c.guideContent:
■ New in v1.11.0: multiple libraries
- Multiple libraries: add as many manga libraries as you like; each one owns its own data directory (database / scan snapshot / thumbnail cache / covers).
- Library switching: group libraries into "switch boxes". Click the toolbar switch button to jump to the next box; the shelf then shows the merged manga of every library in that box.
- Global tags: tags, ratings and titles live in the global metadata.sqlite, independent of which library is displayed.
- Also: recycle bin (deletes go to .trash first and can be restored), per-library cover cache, and SQLite tuned for network shares (no more constant journal create/delete).

■ 1. First run
1. Settings - General - "Data directory" (shared by all libraries): stores settings, tags and metadata (metadata.sqlite), accounts, local models, collections and logs. It takes effect as soon as you press Enter (the client restarts once).
2. "Library locations" (one row = one manga library):
   - Name: rename it to whatever you like;
   - Library folder: read-only, click "Add library" to pick the manga folder;
   - Library data location: where THIS library keeps its database, scan snapshot, thumbnail cache and covers.
     !!! A library only becomes active once this field is filled in. Otherwise it shows "Not active": it is not loaded, not scanned, and cannot be added to a switch box.
     Tip: keep it on a local disk (e.g. D:\emm-data\libraries\manga). The manga files may stay on your NAS, but never put the database on a network share - it is slow and SQLite can be corrupted there.
3. "Library switch" area: one box = one group of libraries. Each click of the toolbar switch button moves to the next box and the shelf shows the merged manga of that box. A box with no library ticked shows every active library. At least one box always remains.
4. Scan: the toolbar scan button (or F5) scans every active library one after another, each into its own database.

■ 2. Tags and metadata
- Tags are stored twice: in each library's database.sqlite (copy) and in the global metadata.sqlite (master). The shelf reads the global copy first.
- Fetch states: non-tag (never fetched) / tagged (fetched) / tag-failed (fetch failed).
- Toolbar "Batch metadata": by default only non-tag books are processed. Tick "Also batch get metadata of tag-failed book" to retry the failed ones too.
- Fetching needs your ExHentai cookie (Settings - General); a proxy and the "request gap" (default 3 s; too small and you get IP-banned) may help. If an IP ban is detected the run stops and the affected books fall back to non-tag so they can be retried later.
- Settings - Tags: categories on top (click to filter) and all tags below. Long-press = favourite, click the colour dot = recolour, X = remove favourite, double-click = rename (applies to every library).

■ 3. Shelf and reading
- The search box understands ExHentai syntax (artist: / c: / p: / f: / m: / language: ...). Sorting and filters include favourites only, hidden only, recently read, plus added/modified/posted time, rating and read count.
- Click a cover for details, click again to read. The toolbar "Switch reader" button toggles between the original reader and ComicRead.
- The reader supports single page / double page / webtoon; the thumbnail sidebar jumps between pages; reading progress is saved automatically; right-click an image to delete it, set it as the cover, or rename it.

■ 4. Recycle bin (undo a wrong delete)
- Deleted manga or images go to .trash/ inside that library's data directory instead of being erased.
- Restore or purge them in Settings - General - Recycle bin; the delete log shows every deletion and which library it belongs to.

■ 5. AI features (Settings - AI)
- Pick local (Ollama) or online (OpenAI-compatible); address, model and key are configured separately.
- Supports: batch title translation, batch information processing (translation + character + parody + artist + category), character origin lookup, image upscaling, and image text extraction.

■ 6. Docker / web version
- Default port 10000. Everything is stored under the mounted /data directory - backing it up is a full backup.
- Desktop-only features (tray, launch at login, LAN browsing API) are unavailable on the web.

■ 7. Interface customisation (Settings - Advanced)
- Toolbar buttons can be added, removed and reordered. Cards can hide title / rating / pages / tags, or show covers only. Cover width and gap are adjustable, as are theme, font and background.
